newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BK official to appeal ruling on UBS share.
newsitem.headline: BK official to appeal ruling on UBS share.

text.p: Peter Hafter, a Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) shareholder who sits on the board of BK Vision, said he would appeal a court ruling that upheld the legality of UBS's plan to introduce a single bearer share.
"I am taking this ruling further, in part for refusing me a legal hearing," Hafter told the Tages-Anzeiger newspaper in an interview published on Friday.
UBS said on Thursday it would introduce the single share immediately if no appeals against the Zurich court's ruling were filed within one month.
UBS shareholders approved the move to adopt a single share on November 22, 1994, but it was prevented from taking effect by two suits calling for annulment.
One suit was filed by BK Vision, UBS's largest shareholder and part of Martin Ebner's BK Group, and the other by Hafter.
A spokesman for BK Vision said on Thursday it was too early to comment on whether it would appeal.
